title: Prefix waterfall benchmark: hit-rate vs memory vs p95 latency under mixed bursts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a deterministic load/benchmark harness that maps prefix-cache hit rate to memory footprint and p95 token latency under realistic mixed workloads and microburst traffic. This ticket scopes the engineering work for a new 'prefix waterfall' sweep: a grid of experiments that vary prefix set cardinality, per-prefix hotiness (Zipf alpha), sequence length mix, and inter-arrival burstiness. The harness must produce tokens/sec, p95 latency, p50/p99, CPU/GPU memory usage, eviction count, and cache fill/eviction traces suitable for regression detection and visualizations.

Design summary:
- Workload generator: supports combination of distributions (Zipf, uniform, bimodal seqlen), temporal patterns (diurnal, microburst Poisson bursts, cold starts), and key churn. Implement as standalone binary with deterministic RNG seeds and config JSON.
- Experiment matrix: sweep over prefix cardinality (1k, 10k, 50k, 200k), hotset ratio (1%, 5%, 20%), batch sizes (1, 8, 64), and two memory caps (default, -30% simulated). Each run records token throughput, p95 token latency, per-prefix hit rate, memory RSS, and KV cache occupancy timeline.
- Observability: emit structured events to our test metrics pipeline (prom/pushgateway + tracing). Metric names: test.tokens_per_sec, test.p95_token_latency_ms, test.kv_hitrate, test.kv_evictions, test.kv_rss_bytes. Include run metadata (seed, config, runtime-commit).
- Regression detection: produce a compact fingerprint per run (hitrate curve + p95 vs memory curve). Register nightly baseline comparisons and alert when p95 regresses >10% at same hitrate or tokens/sec drops >15%. Alerts post to #perf-regressions and create a draft Linear ticket with attached run diff.
- Acceptance criteria: harness runs headlessly in CI for small matrix; produces stable fingerprints (variance <5% for p95 across 5 repeated runs in identical conditions); integrates with the nightly regression job; artifacts linked to PRs.
- Artifacts and export: JSON run output compatible with our existing visualization tooling and a CSV summary for quick lookups.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Simulating memory pressure vs real hardware tuning: we will run both simulated memory caps and a subset of runs on a dedicated machine to validate.
- Workload realism: start with configurable building blocks so product/solutions can add customer traces later.

Implementation plan:
1) Week 1: scaffold generator and basic metric emission; small sanity runs (local).
2) Week 2: build experiment orchestrator that launches multi-config sweeps and aggregates results; integrate with test metrics pipeline.
3) Week 3: regression fingerprinting and nightly job; alerting integration.
4) Week 4: run full matrix on dedicated infra, collect baselines, finalize docs and runbook.

Rollout: land as feature-flagged harness in infra repo; run small matrix on every perf PR (fast mode) and nightly exhaustive sweeps.

Notes: This harness focuses on prefix/predictive caches; it intentionally excludes model micro-architectural kernel changes (those are separate experiments) but should be extensible to instrument kernel-level counters in later phases.
